reason: The hypothesis proposes a deliberate oxidative pre-treatment to engineer a Cr-rich oxide layer on FeNiCrCoCu thin films before wear testing, an intervention not reported in the passages. While the mechanism linking a Cr2O3 layer to improved high-temperature wear resistance is well-established in the literature (P1, P8, P12, P23, P32, P42), the specific application of a controlled pre-treatment to this alloy as a coating, and the direct comparison with an inert baseline, represents a minor but substantive new element beyond simply restating known results.
copied_elements: high-temperature oxidative pre-treatment to form Cr-rich oxide layer
Cr2O3 protective layer improves wear resistance
oxide layer reduces direct metal-to-metal contact and shifts wear to oxidative wear
lower friction coefficient and wear volume with stable oxide film
characterization by SEM, EDS, XPS and wear rate measurement
